deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page has three parts. (A) A small linear-algebra computation that normalises linear forms. (B) Riemann's normal form for a genus-3 curve, the plane quartic. Six linear forms x,y,z,ξ,η,ζ are tied by three linear relations, and the quartic is √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0. Riemann tabulates the special parameter values with labels that look like theta characteristics. (C) A sketch of the general-genus version: a quotient of root functions (Wurzelfunctionen) √x/√y is written as a quotient of theta functions. Here x and y are φ-functions whose zeros are all double. The next page continues (B) in detail.

(A) NORMALISATION OF FORMS.
Riemann writes the forms x+y+z, p: ax+a'y+z, q: bx+b'y+z, r: cx+c'y+z. Beside them he writes the 'reciprocal' forms ξ+η+ζ, (1/a)ξ+(1/a')η+ζ, and so on.
He asks for multipliers p,q,r with p(ax+a'y+z)+q(bx+b'y+z)+r(cx+c'y+z)=x+y+z. Comparing coefficients gives
 p+q+r=1, pa+qb+rc=1, pa'+qb'+rc'=1.
A first attempt is struck out: (bc'-cb')/p=(ca'-ac')/q=(ab'-ba')/r. This is the solution of the homogeneous system pa+qb+rc=0, pa'+qb'+rc'=0. It is not the solution of the inhomogeneous one, which is why it is deleted.
He also starts the analogous quantity for the reciprocal forms, ((1/b)(1/c')-(1/c)(1/b'))/p_1.
He then eliminates p by subtracting the first equation:
 q(b-a)+r(c-a)=1-a, q(b'-a')+r(c'-a')=1-a'.
By Cramer's rule (my completion):
 r = [(b-a)(1-a')-(b'-a')(1-a)] / [(b-a)(c'-a')-(b'-a')(c-a)].
Riemann writes the numerator with the opposite sign, (1-a)(b'-a')-(1-a')(b-a). He expands it as a'b-b+a-ab'-a'+b' and rewrites it as (a'-1)(b-1)-(a-1)(b'-1).
The denominator equals the 3x3 determinant D=det[[1,1,1],[a,b,c],[a',b',c']]; 'bc'-cb'' is noted as its leading term.
So, up to sign convention, r = -[(a'-1)(b-1)-(a-1)(b'-1)]/D, and p and q are obtained by cyclic permutation.

(B) GENUS 3 (RIEMANN'S NORMAL FORM).
The forms satisfy
 x+y+z+ξ+η+ζ=0,
 αx+βy+γz+ξ/α+η/β+ζ/γ=0,
 α'x+β'y+γ'z+ξ/α'+η/β'+ζ/γ'=0.
These six forms, together with √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0, are bitangents of the quartic. This is the form in Riemann's posthumous paper on p=3 (Weber's edition, Werke).
Riemann then lists eight special coincidence cases, each tagged with a sum of symbols:
 Left column: (α β γ) (p+q+r+d); (α 1/β γ) (q+d); (α β 1/γ) (r+d); (α 1/β 1/γ) (p+e+f).
 Right column: (1/α 1/β 1/γ) (p+q+r+e+f); then (q+e+f), (r+e+f), (p+d).
The next page states these conditions explicitly as vanishing determinants, e.g. (1/α 1/β 1/γ)=0 and (1/α β γ)=0, and computes them, e.g. (βγ'-β'γ)+(1/α)(β'-γ')+(1/α')(γ-β)=0. So the transcribed 'α=β=γ=0' etc. is shorthand for these determinant conditions.
The symbols o,p,q,r,d,e,f,ϑ (eight in all) behave like the standard 8-element labelling of the genus-3 theta characteristics: 28 odd ones as pairs, 35+1 even ones from sums of four. My interpretation is that each degenerate case is the vanishing of one even theta-constant, i.e. a hyperelliptic degeneration; this is not certain.
Further lines ('α=∞: p q r e f o; ϑ p r ...'; 'α=a ... die übrigen einf[ach]'; 'x=0: q,ϑ die übrigen einfach') record which labelled bitangents or characteristics coincide and which stay simple as a parameter degenerates. One deleted attempt lists 4- and 5-element sums (q+p+r+e, ...).

(C) GENERAL GENUS p (SKETCH).
Remarks: '0 für 4(p-1) Werthe', 'Verzweigungen 3(p-1)' with the forms (x y z ϑ). Then 'x=0, y=0: p-1 Verzweigung, f_1...f_{p-2}' and 'x=0, z=0: φ_1...φ_{p-2}'. Then '2(p-1) Verzweigungen; 0 für 2p-3 gegebene Werthe'.
The sense (my interpretation): x and y are φ-functions (holomorphic differentials, with 2p-2 zeros) that vanish doubly at p-1 points, so √x and √y are root functions. The f_i (respectively φ_i) are p-2 auxiliary φ-functions tied to the pair x,y (respectively x,z).
The main formula is
 √y·(f_1 … f_{p-2} x(…)) / [√x·(f_1 … f_{p-2} y(…))] = A·ϑ(Σ_α^{2p-2}+x)/ϑ(Σ_α^{2p-2}+y).
In modern terms: a quotient of root functions, corrected by determinant-type factors, equals a constant times a quotient of theta functions. The theta functions have half-period characteristics x and y and are evaluated at a sum of 2p-2 Abel integrals.
The last formula is its multi-point version:
 √(y_1…y_{p-2})·Σ±f_1…f_{p-2}(x y …) / [√(x_1…x_{p-2})·Σ±f_1…f_{p-2}(x y …)].
Here the Σ± are determinants of the φ-functions evaluated at several points. This is an early form of the general theta-quotient / Wurzelfunction determinant formula.
errors: Struck-out ratio (bc'-cb')/p=(ca'-ac')/q=(ab'-ba')/r solves the homogeneous system, not p+q+r=1 etc.; Riemann correctly deleted it.
Numerator of r is written as (1-a)(b'-a')-(1-a')(b-a), the negative of the Cramer numerator; this is harmless as a sign convention, and the later form (a'-1)(b-1)-(a-1)(b'-1) agrees with it.
In the expansion the term a' must carry a minus sign (a'b-b+a-ab'-a'+b'); the transcription '+a'' is either a misreading or a slip.
Part (C) is fragmentary. The counts '4(p-1)', '3(p-1)', '2p-3' and the exact entries of the determinants are not fully specified, so their correctness cannot be checked from the page.

results.what: Solving for multipliers p,q,r expressing x+y+z through three given linear forms (Cramer's rule)
results.modern_name: Cramer's rule / normalisation of coordinates for a set of lines

results.what: Normal form of a plane quartic: six bitangents x,y,z,ξ,η,ζ with x+y+z+ξ+η+ζ=0, αx+βy+γz+ξ/α+η/β+ζ/γ=0, α'x+…=0, and curve √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0
results.modern_name: Riemann's model of the plane quartic via an Aronhold-type set of bitangents
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous p=3 paper, ed. Weber; Weber 1876)

results.what: Eight determinant conditions on α,β,γ,α',β',γ', labelled by sums of characteristic symbols (p+q+r+d, q+d, …, p+q+r+e+f)
results.modern_name: vanishing even theta-constants / hyperelliptic locus in genus 3 in terms of Riemann's parameters

results.what: Quotient of root functions √y/√x (x,y φ-functions with p-1 double zeros) times determinant factors equals A·θ[x](Σ)/θ[y](Σ); multi-point determinant version
results.modern_name: theta quotients as root functions; general-genus determinant (Frobenius–Noether / Fay-type) formula for θ-quotients
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann for the basic idea; Weber, Noether (1880) and Frobenius (1880s) for general p

deep.surprise_reason: The genus-3 normal form and its theta characteristics are well known as Riemann's work (published posthumously via Weber). The sketched general-p determinant formula for theta quotients in terms of root functions is a notable unpublished detail. However, it is fragmentary, and the general idea of Wurzelfunctionen is already attributed to Riemann.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,a1,b1,c1,p,q,r=symbols('a b c a1 b1 c1 p q r'); s=solve([p+q+r-1,p*a+q*b+r*c-1,p*a1+q*b1+r*c1-1],[p,q,r]); D=Matrix([[1,1,1],[a,b,c],[a1,b1,c1]]).det(); simplify(s[r]+((a1-1)*(b-1)-(a-1)*(b1-1))/D)==0

checkable.asserts: the expansion is a'b-b+a-ab'-a'+b', with a minus sign on a'
the reduced 2x2 determinant equals the full 3x3 determinant
the struck-out ratios solve the homogeneous system (p:q:r = bc'-cb' : ca'-ac' : ab'-ba')

checkable.sympy: al,be,ga,al1,be1,ga1=symbols('al be ga al1 be1 ga1'); expand(Matrix([[1,1,1],[1/al,be,ga],[1/al1,be1,ga1]]).det()-((be*ga1-be1*ga)+(be1-ga1)/al+(ga-be)/al1))==0
checkable.asserts: the determinant condition (1/α β γ)=0 written on the next page equals (βγ'-β'γ)+(1/α)(β'-γ')+(1/α')(γ-β)

transcription_corrections: 'α=β=γ=0 (p+q+r+d)' and the similar lines are shorthand for determinant conditions such as (αβγ)=0 and (α 1/β γ)=0, as made explicit on the next page, not literal equalities of the parameters.
In the final formulas the struck item is 'x_{p-2}' / 'y_{p-2}' under the square root, and the Σ± are determinants of f_1…f_{p-2} evaluated at points.
